{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mo-f","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ab7688fa8c3187618e495859f26c24d4b6a785d6325b144ba0d9043796b64036","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mo-class-f:lineage:32","source_registry_sha256":"f128002157e581eb7004b9370c8cfbafd7b29a1596262980704fbda0a45932f5","source_liveness_sha256":"fdf72d02e75b9589fee5aaf5b83ec9705ff03586f574464e3553a827f9b698d8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Missouri pavement markings, traffic officers, traffic signals, sign shapes and colors, and warning signs","heading":"C — Markings, signals and warning signs: line types and colors, no passing zones, stop lines and crosswalks, special lanes, lane rules without markings, traffic officers, steady and flashing signals, left-turn phases and arrows, sign shapes and colors, and common warning signs","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Markings, signals and warning signs: line types and colors, no passing zones, stop lines and crosswalks, special lanes, lane rules without markings, traffic officers, steady and flashing signals, left-turn phases and arrows, sign shapes and colors, and common warning signs
Knowledge domain: what pavement line types and colors mean, where passing and stopping are controlled by markings, how dual-use and shared center lanes work, which lane to use when nothing is marked, when officers override signals, what each steady, flashing and arrow signal means, what sign shapes and colors signal, and what the common warning signs announce. Pictures in these pages are not described; only their written meanings are used.

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
A broken line may be crossed to pass, while a solid line should not be crossed to pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Yellow lines divide traffic going in opposite directions, and white lines divide traffic going the same direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
A yellow line on your left means traffic beyond it is coming toward you, while a white line on your left means it is going your way; a solid white line often marks the right edge of the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
On a four-lane road the center is marked with two solid yellow lines, and you must never cross them to pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
A no passing zone on a two-lane road is marked by a solid yellow line and is placed on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, so finish any pass before reaching it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Do not pass when a solid yellow line is on your side of the center line, and on any two-lane road never pass without seeing enough clear road, even if there is no marking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
When a sign or signal requires a stop, stop before the stop line, or before the crosswalk if one is marked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A02
Yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk or about to step into one, and stay alert at intersections without marked crosswalks, because not every crosswalk is painted. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
In a dual-use lane with turn and straight arrows, you may turn or go straight when both arrows show on the signal, but if only the straight arrow is lit you must wait for the turn arrow before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
A shared center lane, bordered by a solid yellow and a dashed yellow line on each side, is used by traffic from both directions for left turns, or U-turns where allowed, and you turn out of it as soon as your path is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
Never back up in a travel lane; if you miss a turn or exit, keep going to a place where you can safely turn around. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A02
With three or more lanes going your way, stay in the right lane except to pass, but use the center lane if a lot of traffic is entering the right lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A02
On multi-lane roads the left-most lane is meant for passing, and passing on the right is risky because the other driver may not see you and may move over. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Always obey a traffic officer over any sign or signal, so if an officer signals you to stop at a green light, you stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A03
A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and go ahead with caution. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A03
At a steady red light, stop at the stop line, the crosswalk or before the intersection and wait for green unless you are turning right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A03
After a complete stop you may turn right on red if no pedestrians or traffic are in the way, unless a No Right Turn On Red sign is posted. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A03
A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red, so stop unless you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A03
A green light lets you go through, but first yield to vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A03
In a permissive left-turn phase you get a circular green or a flashing yellow arrow and must wait for a big enough gap in oncoming traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A03
In a protected left-turn phase you turn only on a green arrow while oncoming traffic is held by a red light. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A03
A protected and permissive phase alternates between a green arrow and a circular green or flashing yellow arrow, when you must pick a gap yourself. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A03
A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green or a flashing yellow arrow, and you may still need to yield to pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A03
A steady yellow arrow follows a green arrow and warns it will change to a circular green, a flashing yellow arrow or red, so be ready to yield or stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A04
A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn in the arrow's direction, but only after a safe gap in oncoming traffic opens and while yielding to pedestrians. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A04
A green arrow lets you go the way it points, provided you are in the proper lane and no traffic or pedestrians are in your path. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A04
A traffic signal that is dark or not working is treated as a four-way stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A04
Sign shapes carry meaning: an octagon is stop, a triangle is yield, a pentagon is school, a pennant is a no passing zone and a diamond is a warning. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A04
A vertical rectangle is a regulatory sign, a horizontal rectangle is a guide sign, and a round sign or crossbuck means railroad. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A04
Sign colors carry meaning too: red is for stop, yield or prohibited, white and black for regulatory, yellow for warning and yellow green for school. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A04
Orange signs are for construction, green for direction and distance, blue for motorist services, and brown for public recreation and cultural interests. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A05
Warning signs are usually yellow diamonds with black letters or symbols and tell you to slow down and be ready to stop for a hazard or special situation ahead. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A05
A Stop Ahead sign means a stop sign is coming on your road, and a Signal Ahead sign means a traffic light is coming; be ready to stop for either. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A05
At a School Crossing sign, slow down and watch for children crossing, and at a Pedestrian Crossing sign, slow down and yield to people in the crosswalk. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A05
An Added Lane sign means traffic from another road gets its own new lane, so no merge is needed, while a Merge sign means entering vehicles may move into your lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A05
A Lane Ends Merge Left sign means two lanes become one, and a driver in the right lane must merge left and yield to traffic already in the left lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A06
A reverse turn sign warns of two turns in opposite directions, the second possibly sharper, with a recommended top speed of 30 mph or less. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A06
A turn sign marks a sharp turn with a recommended maximum of 30 mph or less, while a curve sign marks a curve whose recommended speed is below the posted highway limit. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A06
An advisory speed plate on a curve or turn sign gives the recommended speed, and you should never go faster than it in rain, snow or ice even if it feels safe in good weather. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F40 | anchor: A06
A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels under 25 mph, as farm vehicles and construction equipment often do. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F41 | anchor: A06
A Slippery When Wet sign warns of a road that gets unusually slick in wet weather, and a Soft Shoulder sign means do not drive off the pavement. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F42 | anchor: A07
Many regulatory signs are white squares or rectangles with black or red letters or symbols covering direction, lane use, turns, speed and parking. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F43 | anchor: A07
A red circle with a red slash over a symbol means that action is not allowed, such as no left turn or no U-turn. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F44 | anchor: A07
A T Intersection Ahead sign means your road ends and you must turn right or left. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

Misconceptions: a flashing yellow arrow does not give you the right-of-way over oncoming cars; a dark signal is not a free pass but a four-way stop; a green light still requires yielding to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection; a traffic officer overrides a green light.
Mnemonics: yellow means yonder, so traffic beyond a yellow line comes toward you, and white means with you; broken line, may pass, solid line, stay put.
Glossary: dual-use lane means a lane marked with both turn and straight arrows; shared center lane means a center lane both directions use for left turns; permissive turn means a left turn made in a gap in oncoming traffic; protected turn means a left turn made while oncoming traffic is stopped; regulatory sign means a sign stating a traffic rule; object marker means a sign flagging an obstacle near the lane.
Dynamic facts: the School Crossing sign is being changed over to yellow green during a transition period, so sign color in the field may vary, and local signal timing and No Right Turn On Red postings differ by location.
